full_judgment: 29. Nextly, about non-production of the two witnesses i.e. investigating officer and the doctor, the reasons are very clear, because it is in evidence that the Investigation Officer Abdus Samad is dead and the doctor Sultan Ahmed has been paralysed and is so invalid that he even cannot speak. For these reasons, they could not be produced in Court. We, of course appreciate the submission of the learned advocate for the appellants that the prosecution may be prejudiced for non-examination of the Investigation Officer or other material witnesses, but in the facts and circumstances of the case when there are reasonable grounds for non-production of the said witnesses particularly when the case is almost admitted by the defence we do not think that any adverse presumption can be drawn against the prosecution case and the non-production of the said witnesses under the above ircumstances are not fatal to the prosecution. In that view of the matter, we are unable to accept the contentions of the learned Advocate for the appellants and we do not find any illegality in the impugned judgment and order of the learned Assistant Sessions Judge and there is no justification to interfere with the impugned judgment and order of conviction of sentence passed on 8.6.89 which should be upheld. At this stage the learned Advocate for the appellants has stood up and prayed for some reduction of the sentence imposed upon the appellants. It is an admitted case that the dispute arose over title and possession of the case-land which ultimately resulted in a mara-mari causing the unfortunate death of the victim Tajur Muluk and that there were litigations still pending over the property between the parties; hence in consideration of all the above facts and the circumstances of the case, we are of. the view that the ends of justice will be sufficiently met if we reduce the sentence of the appellants from ten (10) years RI to 8 years RI each, which is accordingly reduced.
